column1: *Chatbot Arena Elo scores are for text
*MTBench saturated by frontier LLMs with near-perfect results

A large-scale, crowdsourced human preference benchmark where real users compare model outputs head-to-head. The resulting ELO score provides the most reliable measure of overall helpfulness, coherence, and conversational quality.
A high-difficulty math contest benchmark derived from the American Invitational Mathematics Examination. Tool-free evaluation tests pure reasoning ability, not external computation.

A challenging scientific reasoning benchmark containing graduate- and PhD-level questions across physics, chemistry, and biology. Designed to avoid contamination and to measure deep conceptual understanding.

A visual and symbolic reasoning test intended to probe abstraction, pattern discovery, and fluid generalization—key ingredients of AGI-like capabilities. Models must infer rules from examples with no language scaffolding.
A coding benchmark where models must synthesize completions for Python programming problems that pass hidden unit tests. It assesses functional correctness and general code-generation ability.
A broad knowledge benchmark covering 57 academic subjects ranging from humanities to STEM. It tests factual recall, general reasoning, and expert-level domain understanding.

A benchmark designed to measure resistance to producing false, misleading, or commonly believed incorrect statements. Models are penalized for following human misconceptions or generating confident hallucinations.

A real-world software engineering benchmark where models must resolve actual GitHub issues in large codebases. “Verified” indicates automated test execution confirms whether the model’s fix truly solves the bug.
